agentCan: Build the authorization flow (Connect to QuickBooks), per-realmId token storage, and latest-refresh-token rotation
Implement the reconnect flow for the 100-day cliff and revocation events
Monitor CorePlus credit usage against your Partner Program tier

approval.cost: Intuit App Partner Program (all apps are automatically enrolled, listed or not): Builder, no charge, includes 500,000 CorePlus API credits/month ('Any CorePlus calls made above the included monthly credit will be blocked entirely'); Silver US$300/month, 1 million credits; Gold US$1,700/month, 10 million credits; Platinum US$4,500/month, 75 million credits. Core API calls are uncapped; successful (2xx) CorePlus (read-type) calls above a paid tier's included credits incur variable per-1,000-call fees per the rate card. Billing applies at the Workspace level and 'API calls and API Credits are aggregated across all production Apps in a given Workspace'
approval.trigger: Production credentials are locked until the App Assessment Questionnaire is submitted and approved, for ALL apps including private ones. 'All developers with app(s) on our platform, that are connected to one or more production QuickBooks Online companies, need to submit this questionnaire.' 'I have a private app and don't plan to list it on the app store. Do I still need to submit this questionnaire? Yes... The app assessment and compliance process applies to both private (i.e. unlisted) apps and apps that are, or want to be listed, on the QuickBooks App Store.' Before that you must also complete Production Settings (verify email, developer profile, EULA and privacy policy URLs, host domain, Launch URL and Disconnect URL, at least one app category, regulated industries, hosting details). Non-compliance has teeth: 'Refusal to provide the required information or to complete the questionnaire may result in the removal of your app's access to production data.' Assessors expect specific answers about what the app does, who uses it, and its direct relationship to QuickBooks accounting/payments functionality; a 'Requires attention, Security Policies' status is triggered when the described use case does not clearly align. App Store listing is a SEPARATE, optional three-part review (technical, security, marketing): 'Apps need to pass a three part app review before we list them on the QuickBooks App Store', and 'if you don't want to list your app to the QuickBooks App Store, you're free to market your app privately and skip the review'.
approval.wait: Not stated (no assessment or App Store review duration, SLA, or typical wait anywhere in the official docs/FAQ read)

blockers.detail: There is no way to get a production Client ID/Secret without completing Production Settings AND the assessment questionnaire, even for a single-company internal app. Intuit Support, repeatedly: 'If you want client id and secret key for production app, it is necessary to follow publishing the app steps even if it is private app.' Sandbox credentials work immediately but only against sandbox companies.
blockers.howToClear: Start the Production Settings checklist and questionnaire at the beginning of the project, with a use case description that clearly ties the app to QuickBooks accounting/payments functionality.
blockers.title: Production is a one-way gate, not a formality

blockers.detail: 'If a new Refresh Token is returned, the previous one expires' and using a stale one throws invalid_grant; 'always store and use the LATEST Refresh token returned'. Beyond rotation: the refresh token 'can last up to 100 days before it expires' (its value can change every 24-26 hour period), and per Intuit's November 2025 policy change, 'All refresh tokens will now have a maximum validity period of five years' (accounting/payment-scope tokens generated from October 2023 first expire in October 2028). If a refresh token expires, 'the user needs to sign in and grant consent again'; a connection cannot be kept alive indefinitely by refreshing alone. Revocation also kills both tokens: 'If a user revokes connection to the QuickBooks Online company, the access token and refresh token are invalidated.'
blockers.howToClear: Atomically overwrite both tokens on every refresh response, track x_refresh_token_expires_in, and build a reconnect flow before you need it.
blockers.title: Refresh-token rotation, the 100-day cliff, and the 5-year wall

blockers.detail: On the free Builder tier, CorePlus calls above 500,000/month are BLOCKED, not billed: a sync-heavy AI agent can hit a hard stop mid-month. Billing aggregates across all production apps in the workspace, so multiple apps share one meter. Core API calls are uncapped.
blockers.howToClear: Budget CorePlus reads against your tier from the start and monitor workspace-level usage.
blockers.title: Partner Program metering trap for read-heavy agents

flavor.recommended: One production app using the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow, with each customer company running the 'Connect to QuickBooks' flow against your app
flavor.why: The object is an app created in the Intuit Developer Portal, giving a Client ID and Client Secret under the app's Keys & OAuth tab. There is no separate API key: 'There is no such thing as API Key for QBO', and 'Intuit does not support API keys or HTTP Basic Authentication. OAuth 2.0 is the only supported protocol.' Each app has TWO separate credential sets: Development (sandbox companies only) and Production (real companies), not interchangeable. The standard data scope com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting grants full access to the company's accounting data (no read-only or per-entity granularity in the standard scope); com.intuit.quickbooks.payment covers Payments; identity scopes are OpenID Connect (openid, profile, email, phone, address). Restricted and granular scopes (e.g. payroll-related) sit outside the standard self-serve set.

humanMust: Create an Intuit Developer account (you are provided a Sandbox QuickBooks Online company for development and testing)
Create the app and handle both credential sets (Development and Production) from Keys & OAuth
Complete Production Settings (email verification, developer profile, EULA/privacy URLs, host domain, Launch and Disconnect URLs, category, regulated industries, hosting details)
Complete and submit the App Assessment Questionnaire and wait for approval before production keys are released
name: QuickBooks Online
nuances: realmId handling: the company ID is returned only on the authorization callback. Every API call is scoped by realmId (/v3/company/{realmId}/...), tokens must be stored per realmId, and one Intuit user can connect multiple companies, each a separate token set.

Access tokens are valid for 60 minutes (expires_in 3600); authorization codes have a lifetime of 300 seconds (per Intuit Developer Support). Token responses carry x_refresh_token_expires_in (8,726,400 seconds, about 101 days, in Intuit's Ruby SDK example).

Redirect URI strictness: the redirect URI in the authorization request must match the URI registered under Keys & OAuth for that environment; Intuit's Playground troubleshooting calls this out as the most common failure.

Intuit Single Sign-On is optional generally, but 'You need to implement Intuit Single Sign-on if you want your app to appear in QuickBooks Online Accountant'. Intuit refreshes its app compliance criteria periodically, so the assessment is not necessarily a one-time event.
prerequisites: An Intuit Developer account and a Sandbox QuickBooks Online company
EULA and privacy policy URLs, host domain, Launch URL and Disconnect URL for Production Settings
A use case description that clearly aligns with QuickBooks accounting/payments functionality (for the assessment)

steps.detail: 'As a first step, create an account in Intuit Developer portal. Once an account is created, you are provided with a Sandbox QuickBooks Online company on developer.intuit.com that can be used for development and testing.'

links.label: Why do I need to use OAuth 2.0

steps.title: Create an Intuit Developer account

steps.detail: Create an app and select the QuickBooks Online Accounting data source (and optionally Payments). Dashboard > app > Development section > Keys & OAuth: copy the Client ID and Client Secret and register your redirect URI(s) (they must exactly match what your code sends).
steps.title: Create the app; get sandbox credentials

steps.detail: Redirect the user to appcenter.intuit.com/connect/oauth2 with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope (com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting), and state. The user signs in to Intuit, selects their QuickBooks company, and authorizes. Intuit returns code plus realmId (the company ID) to your redirect URI; validate state. Intuit provides SDKs and an OAuth 2.0 Playground for testing.
steps.title: Build the authorization flow

steps.detail: POST oauth.platform.intuit.com/oauth2/v1/tokens/bearer with HTTP Basic auth (Client ID:Client Secret) and the code. Store the access token, refresh token, AND realmId together, per company. Call the API at quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/{realmId}/... with the Bearer token.
steps.title: Exchange the code; store tokens per realmId

steps.detail: Access tokens last 60 minutes. On refresh, overwrite BOTH stored tokens with the returned pair ('always store and use the LATEST Refresh token returned'); using a stale refresh token throws invalid_grant. Build the reconnect flow for token expiry and user revocation.
steps.title: Refresh (latest-token rotation)

steps.detail: Complete the portal checklist: verify your email address, complete your developer profile, add EULA and privacy policy URLs, add host domain, Launch URL and Disconnect URL, select at least one app category, list regulated industries that use your app, and give details about where your app is hosted.
steps.title: Complete Production Settings

steps.detail: Production Settings tab > App assessment questionnaire: answer what the app does, who uses it, and its direct relationship to QuickBooks functionality. Only after approval: Dashboard > app > Production section > Keys & OAuth > copy the production Client ID and Client Secret. All apps are automatically enrolled in the Intuit App Partner Program (Builder tier free with 500,000 CorePlus credits/month).
steps.title: Submit the App Assessment Questionnaire; get production keys

steps.detail: Marketplace section of the portal, listing checklist, and the three-part review (technical, security, marketing). Not required to connect customers: you may market privately and skip it.
steps.title: (Optional) List on the QuickBooks App Store

tagline: OAuth 2.0 is the only supported protocol, but production credentials are locked behind a Production Settings checklist and Intuit's App Assessment Questionnaire even for private apps, and every app is metered under the Intuit App Partner Program. Refresh tokens rotate, die after 100 days unused, and now carry a 5-year absolute maximum.
